title: Private Upgrade Choreography: Agent Preflight, LTS Pin Manager, and Sequenced Rollout Gates
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers need a predictable, low-risk way to receive platform upgrades that can span schema changes, agent versions, and optional feature deprecations. Current ad-hoc upgrade scripts don’t capture cluster state, do not enforce LTS pinning, and lack coordinated rollout gates, causing longer maintenance windows and occasional manual rollbacks.

Proposal: Build a coordinated upgrade choreography that combines an agent-side preflight validator, an LTS Pin Manager to compute allowed upgrade targets per tenant, and a sequenced rollout gate controller that coordinates staged cohorts and automated health gates. The system should produce an auditable runbook, generate preflight snapshots, and provide automated rollback hooks for stateful migrations.

Scope: agent preflight checks, LTS pin rules engine, cohort-based rollout controller, migration snapshot/replay, runbook generation, and integrations with Console rollout UI and on-prem orchestrator. Excludes implementation of migration SQL itself (DB migration runners are separate tasks).
acceptance_criteria: Agent preflight tool runs on customer clusters and returns deterministic pass/fail with a JSON report
LTS Pin Manager accepts a private release manifest and outputs per-customer allowed version ranges
Rollout Gate Controller can define cohorts (by tag/region/size) and progress through gates based on health metrics
Upgrade run creates a snapshot (etcd/kube state + app metadata) and stores it in the customer-provided bucket or our telemetry store
Automated rollback hook can restore the snapshot and revert agent version within the same playbook
End-to-end test coverage with a staged canary run in our lab environment and a documented dry-run checklist
Console shows per-tenant upgrade status and an ordered list of steps (preflight -> migrate -> verify -> finalize)
Security review completed and KMS/HSM integration for snapshot encryption validated
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with RE, Platform, and Support. Agreed owner: Diego Martinez. Identified three critical risks: schema drift, snapshot size, and customer network egress policies.

2026-03-04: Spike complete for agent preflight: prototype collects node health, disk usage, open ports, and current agent version. Early findings: ~12% of lab clusters reported custom CRDs that could affect migration ordering.

2026-03-06: LTS pinning rules drafted. Working model: release manifest declares 'lts' boolean plus minimum-supported previous-major. Pin Manager computes semver ranges and generates allowlist/denylist per tenant tags.
2026-03-08: Design review with Security. Decided snapshots must be encrypted with customer KMS when configured and signed by Redwood key when needed for auditability.

2026-03-10: Implemented first pass of rollout gate controller: YAML-based cohort definitions and webhook-based health checks. Needs integration with telemetry pipeline for per-tenant latency/error SLO checks.
2026-03-11: Support provided a customer case where previous upgrade failed due to heavy KV cache writeback. Added an agent preflight check for cache eviction thresholds.
2026-03-12: PR opened for agent preflight binary and Docker image: gh:redwood-inference/private-upgrade-agent#342. Requesting review from infra and eng-internal-security.
2026-03-13: Dry-run scheduled in lab cluster 'lab-eu-3' for 2026-03-17. Prepare synthetic traffic harness and rollback verification steps.
test_plan: Unit tests: pin manager rules, semver resolution, and gate timeouts
Integration: agent preflight -> runbook generation -> snapshot creation in isolated lab environment
E2E: staged canary upgrade in lab-eu-3 with 3 cohorts, must satisfy health gates for 30m before progressing
Rollback test: induce failure mid-migration and validate snapshot restore + agent rollback within 45 minutes
Chaos test: simulate flaky network and confirm preflight fails with clear remediation steps
deploy_steps: 1) Merge PRs for agent and controller to main and build release candidate
2) Publish agent image to private registry and tag with candidate version
3) Run preflight against lab clusters and record snapshot artifacts
4) Start staged rollout to cohorts defined in YAML (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%)
5) Monitor SLO dashboards and automated gates; if gates fail, trigger rollback hook
6) After successful rollouts, mark release in LTS channel if criteria met
rollback_plan: Trigger: automated gate failure or manual abort from SRE/Support
Action A: Cancel pending cohort promotions and mark release as halted
Action B: Run snapshot-restore playbook (uses previously uploaded snapshot and re-applies agent pod revisions)
Action C: Re-run preflight post-restore to validate cluster health
Action D: Create customer incident with timeline and root cause analysis template
Fallback: If snapshot restore fails, escalate to on-call release engineer for manual intervention
notes: Scope note: This ticket focuses on orchestration logic and safety nets — heavy lifting migrations (DB schema changes) are separate but will be invoked by hooks in this flow.
Operational note: Need to coordinate with Support to whitelist customer buckets for snapshot upload during dry runs
Open question: Do we expose the LTS pin decisions to customers via Console? Proposed: read-only view behind feature flag for 1 quarter.
Security note: Customer KMS integration will require a short-lived grant model; have a meeting with Security on 2026-03-16 to finalize
Metrics: success rate, mean-time-to-rollback, megapayload snapshot size, and preflight false-positive rate
